title: ECTROPION: COMPREHENSIVE CLINICAL ATLAS
summary: An exhaustive guide to the diagnosis, classification, and management of eyelid malposition. This poster details clinical findings, rigorous examination maneuvers for lid laxity, and tiered surgical interventions ranging from punctal cautery to complex horizontal shortening.

sections.title: Clinical Case Presentation & Definition
sections.content:
Ectropion: Eyelid turns outwards, exposing the conjunctiva and potentially leading to eye irritation, excessive tearing, and dryness.

A1. Clinical findings (Description):
• Rt lower eyelid ectropion with chronically inflamed, thickening and keratinization of the marginal conjunctiva.
• Lt pseudoptosis.
• Bilateral inferior periorbital puffiness due to orbital fat prolapse.

rows: Outward turning of the lid margin with conjunctival exposure.
Inward turning of the lid margin; lashes rub against the cornea.
Lid margin is displaced vertically but remains in contact with globe (Thyroid Eye Disease).
Inability to close the eyelids completely; can be a consequence of ectropion.
Easily everted upper lid, associated with obstructive sleep apnea.

branches: History: Trauma or cicatrizing skin disease (OCP, SJS)
History: Previous excision of skin cancer or repair of laceration
Exam: Exposure keratopathy & Bell's reflex (rule out lagophthalmos)
Exam: Location (medial lid, lateral lid, entire lid, punctal eversion only)
Exam: Search for scars or generalized skin tightness
Exam: CN VII Palsy signs (Asymmetry, brow ptosis, no frontal crease, loss of nasolabial fold, mouth angle drop)

rows: Manually pull lower lid away from eyeball
Lid moves more than 6 mm off the eyeball
Pull lower lid inferiorly toward orbital rim and release
Lid fails to spring back into position without a blink
Lateral traction of lower eyelid; observe punctum
Observe appearance and pull lid medially
Round appearance; pulling lid medially > 2 mm

sections.title: Classification of Ectropion
content: LOWER EYELID - Congenital: Rare; associated with blepharophimosis or congenital ichthyosis
LOWER EYELID - Cicatricial: Scarring or contracture of skin
LOWER EYELID - Paralytic: Ipsilateral facial nerve palsy
LOWER EYELID - Mechanical: Lid margin tumours
LOWER EYELID - Iatrogenic: Due to over-correction for entropion

sections.title: Management: Medical Therapy
content: Inducing upper eyelid Ptosis by botulinum toxin injection

rows: Choice for upper lid with floppy eyelid syndrome
Excision of conjunctival diamond inferior to punctum; for punctal ectropion
Thermal cautery of posterior conjunctival surface below punctum
Wedge resection with lateral tarsal strip

branches: Cicatricial (Mild): Z-plasty (excision of scar + vertical lengthening)
Cicatricial (Severe): Transposition flaps or free skin grafts (from upper lids, post-auricular, preauricular, supraclavicular)
Paralytic: Corneal exposure protection (lubricants) + lid shortening
Mechanical: Surgical excision of lid margin tumors + correction of lid laxity

sections.title: Red Flags & Clinical Pearls
content: Rule out basal cell carcinoma (BCC) in any case of localized mechanical ectropion or suspicious lid lesions.
In cicatrizing disease like OCP or SJS, avoid surgery in the acute phase; manage ocular surface aggressively.
Always assess Bell’s Reflex; poor Bell’s with ectropion dramatically increases risk of severe exposure keratopathy.
Keratinization of the conjunctiva (A1 findings) indicates chronic exposure and may require long-term aggressive lubrication.

content.explanation: The Medial Spindle procedure addresses the vertical deficiency and rotation specifically at the medial lid/punctal area by removing a diamond-shaped piece of conjunctiva.
